note: Eval set in the agentskills.io evals/evals.json format. Static assertions are regex contracts over SKILL.md; live assertions need a real repo + gh run and are recorded as not-run (excluded from pass-rate denominators).

evals.prompt: Run /i-pick-issue with no arguments on a repo that has several open issues.
evals.expected_output: backlog map: every open issue listed with number, title, labels and one-line summary, grouped by domain/risk/dependency, a concrete recommended execution order with one single highlighted issue to start. The recommended issue is selected by default and the run proceeds with it unless the operator overrides.

static_assertions.why: every invocation must begin with the Discovery station regardless of arguments
the recommended issue is selected by default, but the operator can always override it
Discovery must present the auto-selected issue and the override path before any station runs
Discovery must prescribe the canonical gh command to fetch the backlog
issues must be grouped logically, not listed flat

static_assertions.pattern: nothing is selected until the operator answers
static_assertions.why: the old halt rule is gone — the recommended issue is selected by default, so the old rule text must not remain
the Discovery recommendation header lives in the output template — SKILL.md must point at it, and the recommended issue is selected by default unless the operator overrides
a catch-all trigger would fire the skill on unrelated conversation

live_assertions: Every open issue is presented with number, title, labels and a concise summary
Issues are grouped logically by domain area, risk, component or dependency chain
A concrete execution order is proposed with exactly one highlighted issue to start
The report presents the recommended issue as selected by default with a chance to override
The recommendation screen does not duplicate itself as a separate 'pick a number' menu
The run proceeds with the recommended issue unless the operator overrides
No planning, building or PR actions are taken before the operator confirms or overrides
The output follows the Discovery report template

evals.prompt: The operator picked issue #42 from the Discovery map. Present the execution mode options.
evals.expected_output: The skill presents exactly two options: step-by-step (halt after each station, recommended) and full orchestration (II→VI end-to-end). It does NOT infer the mode from how the request was phrased and does NOT start Station II until the operator has explicitly chosen.

static_assertions.why: the mandatory mode gate must exist as a named section
step-by-step must be one of the two explicit options
full orchestration must be the other explicit option
the mode must never be guessed from phrasing — always an explicit operator choice

static_assertions.pattern: do NOT start Station II until
static_assertions.why: Station II must not begin before the operator explicitly chose a mode

live_assertions: Exactly two mode options are presented after the operator picks an issue
The mode is not inferred from the phrasing of the request
Station II does not start until the operator explicitly chooses a mode

evals.prompt: Run /i-pick-issue 42 after the operator confirmed issue 42 and chose full orchestration mode.
evals.expected_output: Issue 42 details read and claimed, session scope locked, then sequential hand-off through stations II (plan), III (build), IIIB (iterate), IV (review and PR), V (babysit and merge), VI (close pipeline), with a concise status report per completed station and the next station named.

static_assertions.pattern: Do not claim the issue here
static_assertions.why: Station II owns the first write; Station I must delegate rather than claim
Station II planning must be the first hand-off after assignment
Station III build must follow planning
Station IV review must follow build
Station V merge must follow review
Station VI closeout must be the final station
the router gate must reference pipeline-triage for dirty repos

live_assertions: The issue details are read by Station I, and the claim happens in Station II after its clean-tree check
Station I does not claim the issue itself; it delegates the first write to Station II
Station II planning hand-off produces tasks/plan.md before building starts
Stations run in order III then IV then V then VI with no station skipped
Each completed station is reported concisely with the next station named
No station output contract is broken or silently skipped

evals.prompt: Hey, while you are at it, can you quickly fix the typo in my meeting notes? (unrelated request during an i-pick-issue session)
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger pipeline behavior: no issue listing, no station hand-off, no silent issue pick, no gh commands. Routes to using-agent-skills in one line.

static_assertions.why: the boundary must explicitly exclude ad-hoc requests from Issue work
unrelated requests must be routed to the ad-hoc skill, not silently absorbed

live_assertions: No gh issue command is run for this request
No station hand-off occurs
No issue is picked silently
No files are modified by this request
